display.purpose: Page hero heading and the primary KPI when a page has one. Familjen Grotesk.

headline.purpose: Section titles; page-header title. Familjen Grotesk.

title.purpose: Card titles, list-row primary text. Familjen Grotesk.

body.purpose: Descriptions, paragraph copy, table cells. Public Sans.

caption.purpose: Meta lines under rows, secondary chart labels. Always muted. Public Sans.

label.purpose: Column heads, badge text, uppercase-tracked metadata. Public Sans.

data.purpose: Numbers in tables, chart tooltips, badge counts. Geist Mono, tabular-nums.

data-display.purpose: The big number on a stat tile. Geist Mono, clamp() sized.

scale.eyebrow.purpose: Kicker labels and tiny uppercase tags below Label size.

scale.meta.purpose: Secondary chip text and inline data figures between Label and Body.

scale.chart-figure.purpose: Donut/gauge chart center total figure. Geist Mono.

shadows.name: focus-ring
shadows.purpose: Keyboard focus signal on interactive elements. Never on hover.

shadows.name: overlay-lift
shadows.purpose: Dialogs, popovers, chart tooltips. Never on static cards.

motion.name: duration-fast
motion.purpose: Standard duration for hover, focus, and background transitions.

motion.name: duration-base
motion.purpose: Ceiling for any transition a state change triggers directly.

motion.name: duration-content-arrival
motion.purpose: Named exception to the 150ms ceiling: a cue for content that arrived unprompted, not a triggered state change.

motion.name: rise
motion.purpose: Card/row entrance: fades up from a slight vertical offset.

motion.name: fillbar
motion.purpose: Progress-bar fill animating in from zero width.

motion.name: lift
motion.purpose: Modal or copy-button success settling into place with a slight scale-and-fade.

motion.name: veil
motion.purpose: Modal backdrop fade-in, paired with lift.

motion.name: beacon
motion.purpose: Live-status pulse ring; exempt from prefers-reduced-motion via .motion-safe-pulse.

breakpoints.name: narrow
breakpoints.purpose: Sidebar collapses to top bar below this width.

breakpoints.name: wide
breakpoints.purpose: Second card column enables at this width.

breakpoints.name: ultra
breakpoints.purpose: Stat rows expand from 4 to 6 tiles at this width.

narrative.overview: CC-Track is a control room for a single operator. When the deck lights up, you see three things at once: what is running now, what has been done, and what is still queued. The interface is a status board first, an editor second. Content dominates chrome. On a wide monitor, lanes widen and columns multiply so the deck fills the glass instead of centering a small stage in a sea of margin. The atmosphere is warm graphite: a near-black warm ground with the ambient signal of a workshop lit by a single low lamp. Terracotta is the primary voice raised on that surface, reserved for what the operator should notice next; red is reserved for what went wrong. Numbers speak in monospace so they align down a column; display headings speak in a geometric display sans; everything else speaks in a humanist text sans built for long reading at small sizes. Nothing is playful, nothing is corporate, nothing is empty. This is a working instrument that a person built for themselves and reaches for daily.
keyCharacteristics: Wide-monitor first: fill the deck, do not center a postage stamp.
Big, decisive type; hierarchy carried by size and weight, not by boxes.
One signal color (terracotta) plus four role colors (sage, ember, indigo, red). No decorative color.
Flat surfaces at rest; tonal steps for depth; motion only on state, capped tight.
Data reads in Geist Mono so digits line up without effort.

rules.name: The One Signal Rule
rules.body: Terracotta is the only color that raises its voice for attention. It marks what the operator should look at next: the live session, the CTA, the top of a ranking, the primary chart series. If you catch yourself using it decoratively, replace it with Muted or Text.

rules.name: The Role-Color Discipline Rule
rules.body: Sage means done, Ember means in-flight or warning, Indigo means reference, Red means failed. Never rotate them for palette variety. Rotate through tonal steps of the same role instead.

rules.name: The Alarm-Is-Terminal Rule
rules.body: Red is reserved for a state that has already failed: a FAIL verdict, an error line in stdout. It is not a softer warning color and not interchangeable with Ember. A state in progress is Ember even if it might fail later; only the failure itself is Red.

rules.name: The No-True-Black Rule
rules.body: The Background is warm. Never use #000 on this deck; it flattens the graphite ground and reads as void, not workshop.

rules.name: The Numbers-Are-Mono Rule
rules.body: Any digit that appears next to other digits (stat tile, table cell, chart tooltip, badge count) uses Geist Mono. Prose numbers inside a sentence stay in Public Sans.

rules.name: The Big Type Rule
rules.body: Display and Data Display use clamp() so the deck grows with the viewport instead of stopping at a laptop-era ceiling. Do not cap the deck at 1200px.

rules.name: The No-Em-Dash Rule
rules.body: Copy uses hyphens, colons, commas, or two sentences. Em dash and en dash are banned in every string the app shows.

rules.name: The Relative Unit Rule
rules.body: Every dimension is expressed in rem, em, ch, vw, %, or clamp(). Pixels are permitted only for hairlines under 2px and for box-shadow blur radii. If you are typing a px value greater than 1, stop and convert to rem.

rules.name: The Fill-The-Deck Rule
rules.body: On monitors wider than 1440px, expand content lanes and add columns. Do not center a narrow deck in a sea of margin. Whitespace has to earn its place by carrying rhythm, not by hiding the operator's data.

rules.name: The Content-First Chrome Rule
rules.body: Chrome (sidebar, headers, dividers) uses Line at 0.0625rem. It is present, quiet, and never competes with content.

rules.name: The Flat-By-Default Rule
rules.body: Cards, tiles, and rows do not carry shadows at rest. If a card looks flat and unimportant, fix the type hierarchy or the border, not the shadow.

rules.name: The Tonal-Depth Rule
rules.body: Where a surface needs to feel on top of another, step one tonal level (Background to Surface 1 to Surface 2). Never combine tonal step + shadow at rest.

rules.name: The Warm-Corner Rule
rules.body: Every container uses at least 0.375rem radius. Sharp corners belong to another world.

rules.name: The Radius-Signals-Weight Rule
rules.body: Radius increases with how much a surface floats above the deck: a stat tile (0.875rem) sits flatter than a top-level panel (1.125rem), which sits flatter than a modal (1.25rem).

rules.name: The One-Border Rule
rules.body: A tile has exactly one border: 0.0625rem in Line, or Line Elevated when floating. Nested containers drop the border and rely on tonal step + padding.

rules.name: The 150ms Ceiling Rule
rules.body: No transition triggered by the operator (hover, focus, toggle, filter, tab) may exceed 150ms. No bounce, no scale beyond 1.02, no ripple.

rules.name: The Content-Arrival Exception
rules.body: A cue marking something that arrived unprompted (a new live-timeline row, a progress bar filling in, a card mounting) may run past the 150ms ceiling, up to roughly 900ms. The named exceptions are rise, fillbar, lift, veil, and beacon.

dos: Do express every dimension in rem, em, ch, vw, %, or clamp(). Reserve px for 1px hairlines and shadow blur.
Do let the main lane run uncapped from sidebar to viewport edge, and add columns on wide monitors instead of enlarging margins.
Do put every number that shares a column with other numbers in Geist Mono with tabular-nums.
Do use Terracotta for exactly one thing per screen: the current focus target. Use Red for exactly one thing: an actual failure.
Do pair every colored badge with a word or glyph so color-blind operators still parse state.
Do hover to Surface 2 at 120ms ease-out. Focus-visible gets the Terracotta focus ring.
Do step tonally for depth (Background to Surface 1 to Surface 2) before reaching for a shadow.
donts: Don't use em dashes or en dashes in any string the app shows or any file this project writes. Use a hyphen, colon, or two sentences.
Don't use emoji in UI chrome, empty states, or headers.
Don't introduce gradients on text. Flat, tonal, or hairline text only; subtle surface gradients are the deck's one sanctioned exception.
Don't use #000 for any ground. The graphite is warm; true black flattens it.
Don't animate anything above 150ms unless it is a named content-arrival cue (rise, fillbar, lift, veil, beacon). No bounce, no scale beyond 1.02, no ripple.
Don't center a narrow deck in a wide viewport. Fill the deck.
Don't stack shadows on cards at rest to create depth. Step tonally.
Don't rotate role colors for variety. Sage means done, Ember means in-flight, Indigo means reference, Red means failed, permanently.
Don't cap type at laptop sizes on wide monitors. Display and Data Display use clamp() for a reason.
Don't use zebra striping in tables. Rows are separated by a hairline and by hover state.
Don't use Red for a warning or an in-progress state. That is Ember. Red means it already failed.
